skills: Year 1
Aseptic technique, microscopy and staining until they are reflexes (MIC 101, MIC 105 Microbiol Lab I - the page lists microscopy, staining, cultivation techniques and biomolecule determinations).
Serial dilution and colony counting with the arithmetic written out (MIC 205 Lab II - growth measurement, serial dilution, enumeration).
Basic techniques (MIC 102) and biochemistry (BCH 101, BCH 102) as one picture.
A lab notebook from the first week: dated, in ink, every plate labelled.
Year 2
Microbial chemistry and metabolism you can draw (MIC 201, MIC 202) - the gate to MIC 302, 306 and 308.
Environmental and medical microbiology with real samples (MIC 203, MIC 204) and Lab III (MIC 207).
Molecular biology begins (BTE 207) - the gate to BCH 301, BTE 307 and most 400-level electives.
One outside-major course chosen on purpose: STA 201 now so BTE 317 Biostatistics is open later.
Year 3
Virology, immunology and advanced molecular biology (MIC 301, BCH 301, BTE 307) with Lab IV (MIC 305).
Food, agriculture and pharmaceutical microbiology as quality work (MIC 302, 303, 306): a QC report written the way a factory would read it.
A fermentation run from inoculum to product (MIC 308, if your batch is scheduled for it - see tool 1).
Two electives that point the same way, and a faculty member who knows your name.
Year 4
MIC 450: a supervisor, a question, a notebook of real data, the 7th-semester viva and the 8th-semester defence.
Bioinformatics and genetic engineering you can show (BTE 401, MIC 401).
MIC 400: an industrial or research-organisation attachment and the presentation the department has held for its interns.
A one-page CV, a clean lab-skills list and two recommenders who have seen you at the bench.
dept.career_intro: A microbiology degree is a laboratory degree first: the people who hire you want to know what you can culture, count, identify and prove. The directions below are the common ones; none is a BRACU rule, and the programme page prints no placement list of its own.
careers: Research and higher study
A master's or PhD in microbiology, molecular biology, immunology or public health.
CGPA, a MIC 450 thesis with a defensible result, a poster or paper, two recommenders who know your bench work.
Clinical and diagnostic laboratories
Culture, identification, susceptibility testing and molecular diagnostics in hospitals and diagnostic centres.
MIC 204, MIC 406, MIC 407, BCH 301; BTE 403; organism cards you can recite (tool 5).
Pharmaceutical and vaccine industry
Microbiological quality control, sterility and environmental monitoring, vaccine work.
MIC 306 Pharmaceutical Microbiology, MIC 309, MIC 402 Analytical Microbiology; a MIC 400 attachment in a pharmaceutical firm.
Food, fish and beverage quality
Testing and assuring the safety of what Bangladesh eats and exports.
MIC 302, MIC 403, MIC 307; the QC report card (tool 6); a project with a real processor.
Water, environment and agriculture
Drinking-water testing, environmental monitoring, soil and plant microbiology.
MIC 203, MIC 405, MIC 303, MIC 408, BTE 315.
Fermentation and bioprocess industry
Running microbes at scale for food, enzymes, antibiotics.
MIC 308 (where scheduled), MIC 304, BTE 404 Bioprocess Technology; a fermentation run you logged from inoculum to product.
Public health and epidemiology
Surveillance, outbreak investigation, laboratory networks.
MIC 407 Bacterial Pathogenesis and Molecular Epidemiology, BTE 317 Biostatistics, MIC 204; writing you can hand to a non-scientist.
Teaching and science communication
Schools, colleges and institutes that need someone who can run a teaching lab.
Every lab course, MIC 316 Microbes and Human Civilization, a clear explanation of your thesis to a non-scientist.

The Department of Microbiology page prints "Total Credit Requirement: 136 - 146 Credits", "Duration: 4 Years (12 Semesters)" and "candidates must have Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics in their HSC or equivalent examinations".
Fall and Spring semesters are 14 weeks and the Summer semester is 9 weeks; one credit hour is one 60-minute class per week over a 14-week semester.

MIC 450 Microbiology Project (4 credits, printed "Microbiology Project/Thesis" in the semester table) is taken as 2 credits in each of the 7th and 8th semesters; its marks are Viva-Voce (end of the 7th semester) 15, Thesis/Project Work 55, Defence (end of 8th semester) 30, out of 100.

Elective and outside-major courses are chosen from the courses in the syllabus in consultation with the department.

Students can take a double major with Microbiology as the first major, or Microbiology as a minor; the Minor in Microbiology page lists 27 credits: Core 18 credits (MIC 101, BCH 101, MIC 102, BCH 201, MIC 201, MIC 202), Electives 6 credits (from MIC 203, MIC 204, BTE 207, MIC 302, MIC 304, MIC 306, BTE 401) and Lab 3 credits (MIC 105, MIC 205).

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole Microbiology degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Science in Microbiology as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

The grading scale

A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.

**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.title: Minor and double major
items: The page says a student can take a double major with Microbiology as the first major, or a minor in Microbiology.
